_meta.scope: KBO League (10 clubs) and KBO Futures League (12 teams) as played in 2026, with officially announced or reliably reported changes for 2027 in notes.
_meta.capacity_basis: capacity = largest single-game attendance at that park in the 2026 regular season in KBO official attendance data (= sell-out figure); fixed-seat maxima can be higher.
_meta.dims_basis: Distances/wall heights are from Namuwiki (namu.moe mirror, pages edited Nov 2026) cross-checked with Korean/English Wikipedia and news; conflicts are stated in notes. null = not published or conflicting.
_meta.elevation_basis: Approximate. No published ballpark elevation was found; value is a DEM lookup (Open-Meteo elevation API, Copernicus GLO-90 surface model) at the ballpark coordinates from OpenStreetMap. Surface model includes structures, so treat as +/-10 m.
_meta.see_also: kbo_notes.md in the same directory (rules, formats, sources)

first.notes: Shares Jamsil with Doosan. Largest outfield in the KBO. Capacity 23,750 = 2026 sell-out figure in KBO attendance data. Wall 2.6 m per Namuwiki/ko.wikipedia/Dailian 2026-10-21 (an older Seoul city document says 2.7 m). 2026 was the last season at Jamsil Baseball Stadium (last regular-season game 2026-10-12; park to be demolished, closure listed as December 2026). For 2027-2031 LG and Doosan share a temporary ballpark built inside Seoul Olympic Main Stadium (서울올림픽주경기장, same Jamsil sports complex): about 18,000 seats on levels 1-2 for regular-season games, with the 3rd level openable for 30,000+ at big games/postseason (Seoul city, 2024-07-09); reported field size LF/RF 95 m, CF 124 m (Seoul Shinmun 2026-07-15; another report says 124.5 m), fences to be raised to compensate (height not announced); grass type (natural/artificial) NOT confirmed; official name NOT announced; opening planned for March 2027. A new ~30,000-seat dome is planned on the old Jamsil site for 2032.

first.notes: Shares Jamsil with LG (same field data as the LG record). 2026 was the last season at Jamsil Baseball Stadium (last regular-season game 2026-10-12; park to be demolished, closure listed as December 2026). For 2027-2031 LG and Doosan share a temporary ballpark built inside Seoul Olympic Main Stadium (서울올림픽주경기장, same Jamsil sports complex): about 18,000 seats on levels 1-2 for regular-season games, with the 3rd level openable for 30,000+ at big games/postseason (Seoul city, 2024-07-09); reported field size LF/RF 95 m, CF 124 m (Seoul Shinmun 2026-07-15; another report says 124.5 m), fences to be raised to compensate (height not announced); grass type (natural/artificial) NOT confirmed; official name NOT announced; opening planned for March 2027. A new ~30,000-seat dome is planned on the old Jamsil site for 2032. In the temporary park the clubs keep their current sides (LG third-base side, Doosan first-base side) per Seoul Shinmun 2026-07-15.

first.notes: Only dome in the KBO (fixed roof), artificial turf. Alley distances not published in the sources found (null). Wall 4 m per Seoul city documents and Namuwiki (en.wikipedia says 3.8 m). Capacity 16,000 = 2026 sell-out figure in KBO attendance data (facility maximum for baseball 16,601). Special ground rules for balls hitting the roof are in the KBO league regulations (e.g. a fair ball striking the roof beyond the 3rd catwalk in the outfield is a home run). Also hosts the Futures championship final. No change for 2027 found.

first.notes: Opened March 2025. Asymmetric: LF 99 m / RF 95 m. Right-field "Monster Wall" is 8 m high (length reported as 32 m or 35 m) with a two-level bullpen behind it; the rest of the wall (left to right-center) is 2.4 m. Capacity 17,000 = 2026 sell-out figure in KBO attendance data (maximum incl. standing 20,007). No change for 2027 found.

second_home.notes: 3-game series vs KT scheduled 2026-05-19~21; 2 played (KBO attendance data, 12,120 each), 1 rained out and made up in Daegu. In 2025 also one 3-game series (May 13-15). Artificial turf; LF/RF 99 m, CF 122 m; wall 3 m (Namuwiki only); 12,120 seats. Since the 2025 schedule the KBO board has excluded second-park (artificial-turf) games in July-August (board decision 2024-09-26).

first.notes: Octagonal outfield: straight walls make the power alleys very short (107 m) while the corners either side of center are about 125 m; the most homer-friendly park in the league. Wall 3.6 m including the protective mesh (Sports Kyunghyang 2023/2024; a 2017 article said 3.2 m). Capacity 24,000 = 2026 sell-out figure in KBO attendance data. No change for 2027 found.

second_home.notes: Designated second home since 2014, but Lotte played all 71 home games at Sajik in 2026 (KBO attendance data); in 2025 two games were moved there (Sept 23, 25). Since 2026 it is the home of the Futures club Ulsan Whales. Artificial turf; LF/RF 101 m, CF 122 m; wall 2.4 m; about 12,000 seats (12,048 Namuwiki / 12,088 Wikipedia); expansion to about 18,000 seats planned by the end of 2027.

first.notes: Wall history: 4.8 m until 2021, raised to 6 m for 2022-2024, lowered back to 4.8 m from 2025; per Namuwiki the section in center (under the scoreboard) and near the foul poles is still 6 m. Field enlarged in 2022 (lines 95 -> 95.8 m, CF 118 -> 121 m). Alleys: ko.wikipedia lists 113 m but it is unclear whether that predates the 2022 change, so left null. Capacity 23,200 from 2026 (22,669 in 2025) = 2026 sell-out figure in KBO attendance data. 2027: club still at Sajik. Rebuild plan: main works 2028-2030, reopening targeted March 2031, with Busan Asiad Main Stadium converted to a ~20,000-seat temporary ballpark for use from 2028 (design call May 2026); schedule was still being disputed in late 2026.

first.notes: Alleys left null because published figures conflict: news at opening (Seoul Shinmun 2019) and en.wikipedia give "left-center/right-center 123 m" (the deepest points, just left and right of center, deeper than the 121.9-122 m center), while Namuwiki lists power alleys 107 m plus "left/right of center 123 m". Wall 3.3 m. Capacity 18,128 from 2026 (17,983 in 2025) = 2026 sell-out figure in KBO attendance data. In 2025 the park was closed for weeks after a structural accident and NC used Ulsan Munsu as a temporary home (May 16-22, 2025); not a regular second home. No change for 2027 found.

futures.notes: Military team (players are KBO players doing national service); not a farm team. Moved from the Southern to the Northern League in 2026. 2026: 1st in North, 62-34-0 (.646), 15th straight division title, and won the Futures championship final 8-3 vs Ulsan (2026-09-28, Gocheok Sky Dome).
2026: 2nd in North, 55-46-0 (.545); lost championship semifinal at Ulsan.
Kiwoom farm team, plays under its own name. 2026: 5th in North, 43-59-0 (.422).

2026: 6th in North, 41-60-0 (.406). A new dedicated farm ballpark at Yeongjong (Incheon) was reported in July 2026 as expected to be completed and start operating in 2027; whether 2027 Futures home games move there is NOT confirmed.

New in 2026: first citizen club, founded and run by Ulsan Metropolitan City (KBO board approval 2025-12-09, founding ceremony 2026-02-02); a "Futures League participating club" with no KBO club parent and no draft rights. Squad built from undrafted players, free agents and foreign players (at admission: up to 4 foreigners at max US$100,000 each; limit raised to 6 by the KBO executive committee on 2026-06-02); up to 5 players per season may transfer to KBO clubs. 2026: 1st in South, 58-37-1 (.611); lost the championship final 3-8 to Sangmu. Weekday home games start 18:30. Its status beyond 2026 was being discussed (KBO-Ulsan talks in Sept 2026 on an independent corporation); the club began 2027 preparations in Nov 2026.
2026: 2nd in South, 54-39-1 (.581); lost championship semifinal at Sangmu. A few home games are played at Sajik.
